dimensions.label: Scope
dimensions.reason: In/out is crisp; all optional adjacent items (runbook, LICENSE, branch-alias) explicitly decided and manual provisioning carved out as a human gate.

dimensions.label: Risk
dimensions.reason: Main unknowns are Filament v4 × Laravel 13 resolvability and cross-repo push permissions for the split token — both surfaced with mitigations, both resolved by running CI rather than more discussion.

dimensions.label: Effort
dimensions.reason: ~12 well-understood files across composer config, two workflows, release-please config, and docs; no novel code.

dimensions.label: Clarity
dimensions.reason: Architecture fully specified: release-please (simple, single root component, lockstep) → splitsh-lite split, self.version inter-package deps, non-EOL version matrix.

dimensions.label: Tests
dimensions.reason: Done is defined by a passing non-EOL CI matrix plus a first-release validation that resolves the full chain from Packagist in a scratch project.

problem: markdown-php is a Composer monorepo with three packages — birdcar/markdown-php at the repo root, birdcar/markdown-laravel, and birdcar/markdown-filament — but Packagist serves exactly one package per Git repository. Submitting the monorepo as-is publishes only the core package; the Laravel and Filament packages stay uninstallable. The `composer require birdcar/markdown-laravel` and `birdcar/markdown-filament` lines already advertised in the READMEs do not work for anyone.

There is no release automation, no tags, and no CI. The sub-packages wire themselves together with `@dev` path-repo constraints and `minimum-stability: dev`, which cannot produce stable published releases. The root package is also a dirty publish target: its dist archive would bundle `packages/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, and an unresolvable `spec/` git submodule, none of which a consumer of the core library needs.
goals: All three packages are installable from Packagist by external users via `composer require birdcar/markdown-{php,laravel,filament}`.
Releases are fully automated from Conventional Commits: merging a Release PR cuts a tag, splits the sub-packages, and publishes to Packagist with no manual tagging.
One lockstep version across all three packages, starting at v0.1.0, with inter-package dependencies expressed via Composer's `self.version`.
CI verifies every PHP and Laravel version the composer.json files claim — constrained to currently non-EOL releases only.
The published core package archive is clean: no monorepo scaffolding, no submodule.
successCriteria: Merging the Release PR creates tag v0.1.0 and a GitHub Release on the monorepo.
The split job mirrors packages/laravel → birdcar/markdown-laravel and packages/filament → birdcar/markdown-filament and pushes the v0.1.0 tag to both split repos.
Packagist shows version 0.1.0 for all three packages after the auto-update webhook fires.
In a clean scratch project with no path repositories, `composer require birdcar/markdown-filament` resolves the full chain (filament → laravel → php) entirely from Packagist.
The CI matrix passes: PHP 8.2 / 8.3 / 8.4 / 8.5 × Laravel 12 / 13, run with both --prefer-lowest and --prefer-stable, plus Filament v4.
`composer validate --strict` passes for all three composer.json files.
A downloaded dist archive of birdcar/markdown-php contains src/ but not packages/, docs/, tests/, or spec/.

mvp.item: composer.json release-readiness across all 3 packages: @dev → self.version, drop/relax minimum-stability: dev + prefer-stable
mvp.reason: Without this the packages cannot resolve as stable published releases.

mvp.item: Narrow dependency constraints to non-EOL versions: illuminate/support → ^12.0|^13.0, orchestra/testbench aligned (^10.0|^11.0); keep php ^8.2 (covers 8.2–8.5)
mvp.reason: Laravel 10 and 11 are EOL as of 2026-05-29; the plan should only claim support it tests.

mvp.item: .gitattributes with export-ignore for packages/, docs/, tests/, spec/, .github/, phpunit.xml on the root package
mvp.reason: Keeps the published core dist archive clean and free of the unresolvable spec/ submodule.

mvp.item: release-please config + manifest: simple release-type, single root '.' component, lockstep, bump-minor-pre-major=true, bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major=false, tag format v${version}
mvp.reason: Automates versioning/changelog/tagging from Conventional Commits without touching composer.json version fields.

mvp.item: release.yml: release-please job → split job gated on release_created, re-runs tests, then splitsh-lite via danharrin/monorepo-split-github-action propagating the tag
Reusable tests.yml (workflow_call) matrix + ci.yml invoking it on PR and push to main
mvp.reason: Gates the Release PR and is reused by the split job's re-gate.

phases.title: Package release-readiness
phases.notes: Edit all 3 composer.json (self.version, stability, non-EOL constraints, branch-alias), add root .gitattributes export-ignore, add MIT LICENSE files. Parallelizable with Phase 2 (no shared files).

phases.title: CI test matrix
phases.notes: Reusable tests.yml (workflow_call) matrix — PHP 8.2/8.3/8.4/8.5 × Laravel 12/13, prefer-lowest + prefer-stable, Filament v4 — plus ci.yml on PR/push. Parallelizable with Phase 1.

phases.title: Release automation
phases.notes: release-please-config.json + manifest, release.yml (release-please → split, re-gated, danharrin/monorepo-split-github-action), RELEASING.md runbook.

phases.title: Provision & first release
phases.notes: HUMAN GATE: create the 2 split repos, add the PAT secret, submit all 3 to Packagist + enable the webhook, set branch protection, then merge the first Release PR and verify the full chain installs from Packagist.

execution.agentTeamPrompt: Lead orchestrates four phases for Packagist publishing of the markdown-php monorepo. Dispatch Phase 1 (Package release-readiness — composer.json edits, .gitattributes, LICENSE files) and Phase 2 (CI test matrix — tests.yml + ci.yml) in PARALLEL: they share no files (Phase 1 touches composer.json/.gitattributes/LICENSE, Phase 2 touches .github/workflows/tests.yml + ci.yml). When both complete, run Phase 3 (Release automation — release-please config + release.yml + RELEASING.md), which depends on both. Phase 4 is a HUMAN GATE — do not automate it; surface the RELEASING.md checklist to the user and stop.
